---
title: "Integration"
subtitle: "Definite integrals from samples"
engine: julia
---

Integrals of sampled data, on uniform grids in one to three dimensions and from scattered
points in 2D. The convolution interpolant's antiderivative is built once and a box integral is
then four (or eight) evaluations by inclusion–exclusion; the alternatives are quadrature rules
on the samples (NumericalIntegration.jl), and the exact integrals of spline interpolants
(BSplineKit.jl, Dierckx.jl), applied along one axis at a time in more dimensions. For scattered
points the comparison is a thin-plate radial basis interpolant integrated by adaptive cubature,
since no package integrates scattered data directly.

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Packages, the methods, and the test integrands"
using ConvolutionInterpolations
using NumericalIntegration           # integrate(x, y, rule): Trapezoidal, SimpsonEven, RombergEven
using BSplineKit                     # interpolate(x, y, BSplineOrder(k)) and integral(spline)
import Dierckx                       # qualified: Dierckx also exports `integrate`
import ScatteredInterpolation        # qualified: also exports `interpolate`
using HCubature, QuadGK              # reference integrals, and integration of the RBF interpolant
using Chairmarks, Printf, Random, CairoMakie

# 1D rules: each maps (x, y) on a uniform grid to the definite integral over [x[1], x[end]]
trap_rule(x, y)    = integrate(x, y, Trapezoidal())    # 2nd order
simpson_rule(x, y) = integrate(x, y, SimpsonEven())    # 4th order
romberg_rule(x, y) = Base.CoreLogging.with_logger(Base.CoreLogging.NullLogger()) do   # its convergence warnings are not the point here
    integrate(x, y, RombergEven())                     # high order, needs n = 2^k + 1 points
end

function bspline_rule(k)                               # order-k B-spline interpolant, exact spline integral
    return (x, y) -> begin
        S = BSplineKit.interpolate(x, y, BSplineOrder(k))
        I = integral(S)
        return I(last(x)) - I(first(x))
    end
end

function dierckx_rule(x, y)                            # FITPACK quintic spline, exact spline integral
    spl = Dierckx.Spline1D(collect(x), collect(y); k = 5, s = 0.0)
    return Dierckx.integrate(spl, first(x), last(x))
end

# a 1D rule lifted to N-D by integrating along one axis at a time
function nested_integral(rule, axes::NTuple{N,<:AbstractVector}, A::AbstractArray{T,N}) where {T,N}
    B = A
    for d in N:-1:1
        x = axes[d]
        B = mapslices(v -> rule(x, v), B; dims = d)    # integrate every line along axis d
        B = dropdims(B; dims = d)                      # that axis is gone now
    end
    return B[]                                         # 0-dimensional array -> scalar
end

function conv_query(F, lo, hi)                         # the integral over the box [lo, hi]
    N = length(lo)
    total = 0.0
    for corner in Iterators.product(ntuple(_ -> (false, true), N)...)
        pt = ntuple(d -> corner[d] ? hi[d] : lo[d], N)
        sgn = isodd(N - count(corner)) ? -1.0 : 1.0
        total += sgn * F(pt...)
    end
    return total
end

# the convolution interpolant: the iterated antiderivative once, then inclusion–exclusion over the corners
function conv_box_integral(axes::NTuple{N,<:AbstractVector}, A::AbstractArray{T,N}; kernel = :b7) where {T,N}
    grid = N == 1 ? axes[1] : axes
    F = convolution_interpolation(grid, A; kernel = kernel, derivative = -1)
    return conv_query(F, first.(axes), last.(axes))
end

methods = [
    "Trapezoid"        => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(trap_rule, axes, A),
    "Simpson"          => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(simpson_rule, axes, A),
    "Romberg"          => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(romberg_rule, axes, A),
    "Dierckx k=5"      => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(dierckx_rule, axes, A),
    "BSplineKit k=4"   => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(bspline_rule(4), axes, A),
    "BSplineKit k=8"   => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(bspline_rule(8), axes, A),
    "ConvInterp :b7"   => (axes, A) -> conv_box_integral(axes, A; kernel = :b7),
    "ConvInterp :b13"  => (axes, A) -> conv_box_integral(axes, A; kernel = :b13),
]

# the test integrands and their reference integrals
g(x) = exp(x) * cos(4x) + 1 / (1 + 16 * (x - 0.4)^2)   # smooth, non-polynomial, non-periodic
I_g = quadgk(g, 0.0, 1.0; rtol = 1e-14)[1]              # 1D reference
f_sep(p...) = prod(g, p)                                # separable N-D integrand, reference I_g^N
f2(x, y) = exp(-3 * (x - 0.4)^2 - 2 * (y - 0.6)^2) * cos(4 * x * y + y)   # non-separable 2D integrand
I_f2 = hcubature(p -> f2(p[1], p[2]), [0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0]; rtol = 1e-13)[1];
```

The integrands are $g(x) = e^x \cos 4x + 1/(1 + 16(x - 0.4)^2)$, products of it in more
dimensions, and a non-separable Gaussian-times-cosine in 2D; the references come from adaptive
quadrature at tolerance $10^{-13}$ and below.

## Convergence

The relative error of each method against the number of points per axis, on grids of
$2^k + 1$ points so that Romberg's rule applies:

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "The convergence study"
function run_uniform(N, ns, methods, f, I_ref)
    errs = Dict(name => Float64[] for name in first.(methods))
    for n in ns
        axes = ntuple(_ -> range(0.0, 1.0; length = n), N)
        A = [f(p...) for p in Iterators.product(axes...)]
        for (name, m) in methods
            push!(errs[name], abs(m(axes, A) - I_ref) / abs(I_ref))
        end
    end
    return errs
end

ns_1d = [9, 17, 33, 65, 129, 257]
ns_2d = [9, 17, 33, 65, 129]
ns_3d = [9, 17, 33, 65]                                # 65³ = 274 625 samples, the most expensive case

errs_1d = run_uniform(1, ns_1d, methods, f_sep, I_g^1)
errs_2d = run_uniform(2, ns_2d, methods, f_sep, I_g^2)
errs_3d = run_uniform(3, ns_3d, methods, f_sep, I_g^3)
errs_2n = run_uniform(2, ns_2d, methods, f2, I_f2)

cases = [("1D, separable", ns_1d, errs_1d), ("2D, separable", ns_2d, errs_2d),
         ("3D, separable", ns_3d, errs_3d), ("2D, non-separable", ns_2d, errs_2n)]
fig = Figure(size = (800, 1200))
for (i, (title, ns, errs)) in enumerate(cases)
    ax = Axis(fig[i, 1]; xscale = log10, yscale = log10, title = title,
              xlabel = "points per axis", ylabel = "relative error")
    for (name, _) in methods
        scatterlines!(ax, ns, max.(errs[name], 1e-17); markersize = 8, label = name)
    end
    Legend(fig[i, 2], ax)
end
fig
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# the observed order over the last refinement of each case that is clear of the method's floor:
# both of its errors at least ten times the error at the finest grid, so that a segment ending
# on the floor is never measured; for a method that has not reached a floor, the last refinement
function observed(errs, ns, name)
    e = errs[name]
    j = findlast(j -> e[j] > 10 * e[end], 2:length(e))
    j = j === nothing ? length(e) : j + 1
    h1, h2 = 1 / (ns[j-1] - 1), 1 / (ns[j] - 1)
    return log(max(e[j-1], 1e-17) / max(e[j], 1e-17)) / log(h1 / h2)
end
cases = [("1D", errs_1d, ns_1d), ("2D", errs_2d, ns_2d), ("3D", errs_3d, ns_3d), ("2D non-separable", errs_2n, ns_2d)]
println("| Observed order | ", join(first.(cases), " | "), " |")
println("|:--|", "--:|"^length(cases))
for (name, _) in methods
    println("| ", name, " | ", join((@sprintf("%.2f", observed(e, n, name)) for (_, e, n) in cases), " | "), " |")
end
```

Each order is measured on the last refinement before the method's floor, so a method that has
reached rounding is reported at the rate it converged, not at the floor.

## Scattered points

Points scattered in the unit square, the non-separable integrand sampled at them without
noise, and the integral over the points' bounding box. The convolution route is the exact
scattered fit with `derivative = -1`, which gives the antiderivative interpolant directly; the
alternative is a thin-plate radial basis interpolant integrated by adaptive cubature, which
costs a dense solve and one interpolant evaluation per cubature point:

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "The scattered-data comparison"
function scattered_comparison(f, n_list; seed = 1)
    rng = MersenneTwister(seed)
    rows = NamedTuple[]
    for npts in n_list
        pts = rand(rng, 2, npts)                                   # columns are points in [0, 1]²
        vals = [f(pts[1, i], pts[2, i]) for i in 1:npts]
        lo = [minimum(pts[1, :]), minimum(pts[2, :])]
        hi = [maximum(pts[1, :]), maximum(pts[2, :])]
        I_ref = hcubature(p -> f(p[1], p[2]), lo, hi; rtol = 1e-13)[1]

        t0 = time_ns()
        F = convolution_interpolation(pts, vals; mode = :exact, derivative = -1)
        I_conv = conv_query(F, lo, hi)
        t_conv = (time_ns() - t0) / 1e9

        t0 = time_ns()
        rbf = ScatteredInterpolation.interpolate(ScatteredInterpolation.ThinPlate(), pts, vals)
        I_rbf = hcubature(p -> ScatteredInterpolation.evaluate(rbf, reshape(p, 2, 1))[1],
                          lo, hi; rtol = 1e-10, maxevals = 500_000)[1]
        t_rbf = (time_ns() - t0) / 1e9

        push!(rows, (n = npts, e_conv = abs(I_conv - I_ref) / abs(I_ref), t_conv = t_conv,
                     e_rbf = abs(I_rbf - I_ref) / abs(I_ref), t_rbf = t_rbf))
    end
    return rows
end
scattered_rows = scattered_comparison(f2, [500, 1000, 2000]);
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
println("| points | ConvInterp error | ConvInterp time | thin-plate RBF + cubature error | RBF time |")
println("|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|")
for r in scattered_rows
    @printf("| %d | %.1e | %.2f s | %.1e | %.2f s |\n", r.n, r.e_conv, r.t_conv, r.e_rbf, r.t_rbf)
end
```

## Setup and query

The antiderivative interpolant is built once; after that a definite integral over any sub-box
is a few evaluations, independent of the grid size. Of the alternatives, BSplineKit (1D) and
Dierckx's `Spline2D` (2D) have a comparable split between setup and query; the quadrature
rules have no reusable setup, and integrate grid-aligned boxes only.

```{julia}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "The timings"
function timing_rows(N, ns, f; kernel = :b7)
    rng = MersenneTwister(2)
    rows = NamedTuple[]
    for n in ns
        axes = ntuple(_ -> range(0.0, 1.0; length = n), N)
        A = [f(p...) for p in Iterators.product(axes...)]
        grid = N == 1 ? axes[1] : axes
        lo = ntuple(_ -> 0.1 + 0.3 * rand(rng), N)     # one random sub-box, shared by every method
        hi = ntuple(_ -> 0.6 + 0.3 * rand(rng), N)

        t_setup = (@b convolution_interpolation($grid, $A; kernel = $kernel, derivative = -1)).time
        F = convolution_interpolation(grid, A; kernel = kernel, derivative = -1)
        t_query = (@b conv_query($F, $lo, $hi)).time

        t_s = t_q = NaN
        if N == 1
            x = axes[1]
            t_s = (@b integral(BSplineKit.interpolate($x, $A, BSplineOrder(8)))).time
            I = integral(BSplineKit.interpolate(x, A, BSplineOrder(8)))
            t_q = (@b $I($(hi[1])) - $I($(lo[1]))).time
        elseif N == 2
            x, y = collect(axes[1]), collect(axes[2])
            t_s = (@b Dierckx.Spline2D($x, $y, $A; kx = 5, ky = 5, s = 0.0)).time
            spl = Dierckx.Spline2D(x, y, A; kx = 5, ky = 5, s = 0.0)
            t_q = (@b Dierckx.integrate($spl, $(lo[1]), $(hi[1]), $(lo[2]), $(hi[2]))).time
        end
        push!(rows, (n = n, t_setup = t_setup, t_query = t_query, t_s = t_s, t_q = t_q))
    end
    return rows
end
timings = [(1, "BSplineKit k=8", timing_rows(1, ns_1d, f_sep)),
           (2, "Dierckx k=5", timing_rows(2, ns_2d, f_sep)),
           (3, "", timing_rows(3, ns_3d, f_sep))];
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
fmt(t) = isnan(t) ? "—" :
         t < 1e-6 ? @sprintf("%.0f ns", 1e9 * t) :
         t < 1e-3 ? @sprintf("%.1f μs", 1e6 * t) :
         t < 1    ? @sprintf("%.2f ms", 1e3 * t) : @sprintf("%.2f s", t)
for (N, other, rows) in timings
    println("\n**$(N)D**, kernel `:b7`", isempty(other) ? " (no competitor with a reusable setup)" : " against $other", "\n")
    println("| points per axis | ConvInterp setup | ConvInterp query | $(isempty(other) ? "" : other * " setup") | $(isempty(other) ? "" : other * " query") |")
    println("|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|")
    for r in rows
        println("| ", r.n, " | ", fmt(r.t_setup), " | ", fmt(r.t_query), " | ", fmt(r.t_s), " | ", fmt(r.t_q), " |")
    end
end
```

The query column is the point: once the interpolant exists, an integral over any box costs
microseconds whatever the grid, in any dimension. The setup grows with the grid, as any
interpolant's does, and the 3D rows show it is still the only route with a reusable setup
there.
